title: Stop the slicing
description:
`chorus` is meant to return what every animal says. It takes a `std::vector<Animal>`: a vector of **base objects by value**. Putting a `Dog` in there copies only its `Animal` part; the dog-ness is sliced off, and everything says `"..."`.

Change `chorus` to take a `const std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Animal>>&` so that the real objects are kept. The body needs one small change to match.

For two dogs and a cat it should return `"Woof Woof Meow"`.
